US President Donald J. Trump has launched his most dangerous act of aggression
yet on the world stage. Posterity will be taking copious notes on how the
world responds.

Trump’s illegal February 28, 2026, attack on Iran came after he offered the
Trojan horse of [sham
“diplomacy”](https://www.jurist.org/commentary/2026/03/how-the-trump-
administrations-iran-strategy-backfired-a-breach-of-diplomatic-trust/) to de-
escalate a [purported](https://truthout.org/articles/us-war-on-iran-is-not-
about-nuclear-threats-its-about-us-power-and-
domination/?gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=437238503&gclid=Cj0KCQiAk6rNBhCxARIsAN5mQLvBXV6I3tg3He0F8dmMXJoQYw87pr6nzA_HZlpCg0X3d3OPi3gVx7waAtuSEALw_wcB)
nuclear threat to the US. His action was a blatant attempt to “[wag the
dog](https://www.mediaite.com/opinion/wagging-the-dog-trump-bombed-iran-and-
blew-up-his-america-first-base/),” aiming to
[distract](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/mar/07/trump-iran-hype-
videos?CMP=Share_iOSApp_Other) from [damning revelations implicating
him](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/feb/26/trump-epstein-files-fbi)
in the Epstein files and his [waning popularity at
home](https://www.chathamhouse.org/2026/01/donald-trumps-poll-numbers-suggest-
his-popularity-waning) ahead of the mid-term elections. He aspires to more
control of global [oil
resources](https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/2026/03/04/trump-us-oil-
tankers-iran-war/) and to [cater to his religious
fundamentalist](https://www.militaryreligiousfreedom.org/2026/03/mrff-
inundated-with-complaints-of-gleeful-commanders-telling-troops-iran-war-is-
part-of-gods-divine-plan-to-usher-in-the-return-of-jesus-
christ/?fbclid=IwZnRzaAQUg11leHRuA2FlbQIxMQBzcnRjBmFwcF9pZAo2NjI4NTY4Mzc5AAEexASK3LomYbUjYvhedhK7tHjsCVCTnP73eIFSZtad1pkcElmhXio5GUIG4S4_aem_ENWNHWeJ-1PWei9zAWrDHQ)
base. Trump’s incursion accordingly lacks any reasonable
[endgame](https://theintercept.com/2026/03/05/trump-iran-war-plan-cia/)
strategy for Iran. None of this should come as a surprise given Trump’s
record. Just weeks ago, he ordered the [unlawful “rendition” of Nicolás
Maduro](https://www.thenation.com/article/world/trump-maduro-war-venezuela-
regime-change/) from Venezuela for similar reasons.

Trump has veiled his latest actions in humanitarian dissimulation. At the
center of his [opportunistic deflection](https://www.haaretz.com/us-
news/2026-03-05/ty-article/.premium/why-trumps-fantasies-for-iran-go-far-
beyond-regime-change/0000019c-be22-d521-a7fd-feb6f6540000) is his claim to
care about the liberation of the Iranian people from what is undeniable
suffering at the hands of the reprehensible rule of the Ayatollahs. That
regime’s recent [repressive massacring](https://time.com/7357635/more-
than-30000-killed-in-iran-say-senior-officials/) of tens of thousands of
courageous Iranian protesters created the [perfect
storm](https://truthout.org/articles/what-are-the-trump-administrations-true-
objectives-in-iran/) for Trump to initiate his nefarious plan.

On cue, Machiavellian Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu [seized the
opportunity](https://www.haaretz.com/opinion/2026-03-03/ty-article-
opinion/.premium/netanyahu-hopes-the-iran-war-can-secure-him-the-elections-
casualties-be-damned/0000019c-afe5-df64-a59c-eff70e4f0000) to once again “pre-
emptively” attack Iran to lift his falling poll numbers ahead of the upcoming
Israeli election, in which a victory would help him [stay out of
jail](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/nov/30/benjamin-netanyahu-asks-
israel-president-isaac-herzog-for-pardon-corruption-
case?cmp=share_iosapp_other). As with the American onslaught, Israeli
aggression is not about bringing liberty to the Iranian people. Netanyahu’s
government does not wish for a free Iran; on the contrary, it hopes for a weak
Iran that can no longer pose a threat to Israel. The resulting assault has led
to predictable reprisals from Iran and its allies. As the United States and
Israel respond to each of these retaliations in kind, the cycle of violence
and killing escalates with no end in sight. It will continue to reignite old
hatreds and birth new appetites for revenge on all sides.

Like each of us, I have a responsibility to myself, my children, and our
descendants to explain where I stand at this fraught moment, as the world
descends into an abyss. Make no mistake: no matter how this precarious
situation ultimately unfolds, posterity will be paying close attention to how
onlookers respond, whether with staunch support, tacit endorsement, [complicit
silence](https://truah.org/resources/michael-zoosman-yom-hashoah-
moraltorah_2025_/), or firm opposition.

**Operations “Epic Fury” and “Roaring Lion” Teach Expressly the Wrong Lesson**

I am an ordained Jewish cantor and[ Progressive
Zionist](https://ameinu.net/about-ameinu/progressive-zionism/) who [loves the
people and land of Israel](https://blogs.timesofisrael.com/marching-for-life-
at-the-march-for-israel/) and who is fully cognizant of the existential threat
that the Iranian theocracy presents for them and the world. Nevertheless,
allow me to be abundantly clear: I am wholeheartedly opposed to the criminal
acts of aggression against Iran that the United States has dubbed “Operation
Epic Fury,” and that Israel calls “Operation Roaring Lion.” I similarly
[publicly denounced](https://blogs.timesofisrael.com/two-wrongs-never-make-a-
right-why-i-oppose-the-pre-emptive-attacks-on-iran/) Israel’s June, 2025
“Operation Rising Lion” campaign, which targeted Iran for equally fallacious
reasoning. I repeat what I exhorted then: two wrongs never make a right.

I have [come to
understand](https://www.jurist.org/commentary/2024/02/rethinking-an-eye-for-
an-eye-a-journey-towards-death-penalty-abolition/) the lethal implications of
that deceptively [simple lesson](https://blogs.timesofisrael.com/mr-rogers-
and-the-death-penalty/) in my work as an activist striving to end the vengeful
practice of capital punishment. Just as that lesson applies to Israel’s
[genocidal acts](https://www.jurist.org/commentary/2025/09/veiled-vengeance-
from-the-death-penalty-to-the-gaza-genocide/) in Gaza in response to the
horrific Hamas terrorist attack of October 7, 2023, so, too, does it apply to
Trump and Netanyahu’s latest military offensive against Iran.

Even if, [against all odds](https://www.haaretz.com/middle-east-
news/iran/2026-03-07/ty-article-live/iranian-barrage-triggers-sirens-in-
central-israel-as-idf-raids-eastern-
lebanon/0000019c-c6ac-d2c4-afde-f6ee67ff0000), the current conflict leads to
regime change and does not snowball into a broader regional war, the ends of
this offensive do not justify the means. It may be that [Mojtaba
Khamenei](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/world/article-iran-mojtaba-khamenei-
new-supreme-leader/), or any subsequent ayatollah that the mullahs (or [Trump
himself](https://open.substack.com/pub/heathercoxrichardson/p/march-5-2026?r=1vxpzi&utm_medium=ios))
elect, will miraculously change course from Ali Khamenei’s violent fanaticism.
Alternatively, the hoi polloi might still somehow manage to topple the
government once and for all. Then again, perhaps the incursion will be over in

says-iran-war-projected-to-last-4-to-5-weeks-could-go-far-longer) as per
Trump’s already
[recanted](https://www.democracynow.org/2026/3/3/mortazavi_iran_middle_east_troops_war?utm_source=Democracy+Now%21&utm_campaign=f9d10d455f-Daily_Digest_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_fa2346a853-f9d10d455f-193077215)promise.
(That fantastical timetable is contrary to many signs on the ground, including
the Pentagon’s [preparations](https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/pentagon-
prepares-israeli-us-war-iran-could-last-until-september-report) for continuing
war through September and the [opening of new
fronts](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/aug/21/iran-backed-militia-
blames-us-and-israel-on-bases-in-iraq) in the ever-expanding conflict.) Maybe,
once this campaign’s dust eventually settles, the world will be safer, with a
saner governing model at Iran’s helm.

Still, none of these outcomes would legitimize Trump and Netanyahu’s
manifestly illicit actions. Every ship that the US and Israel
[sink](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/mar/04/us-submarine-torpedo-
iran-warship-sri-lanka-coast-pete-hegseth?CMP=Share_iOSApp_Other), each
[jet](https://www.timesofisrael.com/in-world-1st-israeli-f-35-shoots-down-
iranian-jet-in-air-to-air-combat-over-
tehran/?utm_source=The+Daily+Edition&utm_campaign=daily-
edition-2026-03-04&utm_medium=email) they shoot down, and any tactical
advantage they gain in this war only further deepens the grave they dig for
the prospect of gaining the moral high ground and halting the cycle of
killings that their very actions fuel.

Regrettably, countless individuals feel otherwise. Some
[conclude](https://blogs.timesofisrael.com/yes-israels-war-with-iran-is-
legal/) that Trump and Netanyahu’s acts of aggression in Iran are legal and
appropriate responses to Iran’s deplorable history of proxy wars and direct
missile attacks. Others specifically misapply international law, erroneously
[citing](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/politics/article-canada-announces-
iran-sanctions/) it as a justification for this unprovoked attack. Their
errors are perilous, at best; catastrophic, at worst. Their failure to hold
the ethical line in this pivotal moment endangers the international rule of
law.

There are, of course, occasions that do legally justify war. I myself would
have enlisted to fight against Hitler, Napoleon, and other aggressors
throughout history. This latest foray into Iran, despite the real threat that
the regime poses, categorically does not qualify. The vast majority of
international political and legal scholars
[agree](https://theconversation.com/neither-preemptive-nor-legal-us-israeli-
strikes-on-iran-have-blown-up-international-
law-277173#:~:text=Article%202\(4\)%20of%20the,International%20Atomic%20Energy%20Agency%20affirmed.)that
it is an [obvious abrogation of international humanitarian
law](https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/mar/01/trump-and-
netanyahus-attack-on-iran-is-an-act-of-aggression).

**Empathizing with Victims of the Iranian Regime**

Before returning to the legal case, it is worth pausing on the human one.
Those of us who oppose this attack must remember that many individuals whom
the Iranian regime has harmed have legitimate reasons for welcoming the
assault. One can only imagine how those with victimized loved ones would
celebrate the attacks that began on February 28. As a dedicated death penalty
abolitionist, I am [keenly aware](https://blogs.timesofisrael.com/lchaim-
demands-increased-press-coverage-of-global-executions/) of the mortal danger
that Iranian mullahs have posed for their own citizens through the use of
politically-motivated capital punishment, including public hangings, and other
barbaric “criminal justice” practices. Examples include the state killings of
Iranian Jews like [Nethanel ben Ziona
Ghahremani](https://blogs.timesofisrael.com/statement-from-lchaim-on-irans-
execution-of-a-jewish-man-for-self-defense/), (of blessed memory), who Iran
put to death for a clear act of self-defense, and of non-Jews like [Mahsa
Amini](https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-68511112), (of blessed
memory), whose unjustifiable murder at the hands of Iranian authorities
sparked the “Woman, Life, Freedom” movement. I have many dear Iranian friends
who have been applauding these efforts to “liberate” their homeland.

We should extend the same latitude to individuals in the line of Iranian fire
in Israel and in other locations throughout the Middle East. If I were living
in Israel or if the Iranian government had targeted my own family, I, too,
likely would welcome the recent attacks on Iran. I therefore do not judge
anyone whose loved ones the Iranian regime has assailed. The world has a
responsibility to balance protecting these individuals’ needs as much as
possible while observing international law. Trump and Netanyahu’s gamble
rejects that balance entirely.

There are no so-called “good guys” in this conflict. Neither can there be two
sets of rules: not for Trump and Netanyahu, nor for my fellow Jews and Gentile
neighbors. It is more imperative than ever for civilized humanity to cling to
the underlying ethical standards that hold us afloat, however delicately. The
world must continue to seek to remove the threat of the current Iranian regime
legally and justly through continued binding negotiation.

**“The March of Folly”**

The illegal actions of megalomaniacs like Trump and Netanyahu serve as but the
latest installment in what acclaimed historian Barbara Tuchman has dubbed
[“The March of Folly: From Troy to
Vietnam,”](https://fivebooks.com/book/march-folly-by-barbara-w-tuchman/)
namely, humanity’s repeated pattern of amassing more wrongs in the purported
attempt to make things right. History may assert that I am incorrect in
applying this calculus here; yet, it is often the victors who write history.
No matter how the history books ultimately frame it, Trump and Netanyahu’s
recent deadly strikes were politically-motivated attacks that rationalized
war-mongering under the grossly misapplied flag of “self-defense.” It is moot
to ask whether it was strategically advantageous to attack Iran when it was
weak and isolated; the ethical argument must always outweigh the strategic
one.

“Ethics.”

“International humanitarian law.”

“Human rights.”

These terms all matter. They are not simply words on a page or ideas to ponder
or heed when convenient. They serve as underpinnings to the rule of law.
Society ignores that law and these foundational values at its peril. Doing so
leaves an opening for others to manipulate for their own felonious ends.

I have a [responsibility as a global citizen and proud
Jew](https://blogs.timesofisrael.com/when-human-rights-become-too-political/)
to do my part to uphold the evolving standards of human rights that I believe
my spiritual tradition has been striving to carve out since its founding. To
remain silent or [toe the party
line](https://www.jurist.org/commentary/2024/01/my-fellow-jewish-leaders-
should-not-toe-the-party-line-on-israel/) in the face of the erosion of this
ethical thin red line is to be complicit in its destruction. To do so strains
credulity, especially now, when opening salvos in this conflict have already
resulted in well over eleven hundred Iranian civilian deaths in
[Iran](https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/mar/02/civilian-
deaths-in-iran-pass-200-amid-fear-of-bombs-and-regime-
clampdown?CMP=Share_iOSApp_Other), a devastating majority of the roughly
thirteen hundred reported deaths thus far.

As of this writing, just over a week into this war, that death toll includes
168 seven-to-twelve-year-old girls and staff at[ Shajareh
Tayyebeh](https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/mar/03/minab-
school-bombing-how-the-worst-mass-casualty-event-of-the-iran-war-unfolded-a-
visual-guide?CMP=Share_iOSApp_Other), a [bombed-out primary
school](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/3/3/iran-holds-mass-funeral-for-
girls-staff-killed-in-us-israel-school-attack) in Minab, and mounting deaths
from other retaliatory attacks in
[Israel](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c363zkp1pgxo) and [across the
Middle East](https://www.forbes.com/sites/sofiachierchio/2026/03/02/these-
countries-besides-us-israel-dubai-oman-report-deaths-from-irans-retaliation-
strikes/). This tally says nothing of the deaths of combatants, including at
least [seven American soldiers killed](https://www.haaretz.com/middle-east-
news/iran/2026-03-08/ty-article-live/idf-says-it-hit-several-iranian-fuel-
depots-destroyed-hezbollah-rocket-
launcher/0000019c-ca67-db5a-a99f-db6734190006), with many more on all sides of
this conflict likely to follow. Meanwhile, hospitals across the region
overflow with the wounded. This war has also
[displaced](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/mar/06/us-israel-threaten-
major-escalation-airstrikes-iran-lebanon?CMP=Share_iOSApp_Other) over a

for flexibility, even bending the “rules of war” when adhering to such ideals

bellum_ (justification for war) when human lives are at stake is not viable,
by definition.

**Sounding the Alarm for Future Generations, no Matter the Cost**

I recently reposted a
[statement](https://www.facebook.com/share/p/1C9QMkXanE/?mibextid=wwXIfr) on
social media from [T’ruah: The Rabbinic Call for Human
Rights](https://truah.org/) that stridently opposes the illegitimate attack
against Iran. In response, a fellow Jewish clergyperson who endorses the
assaults on Iran stated disparagingly that future generations will remember
where I stood in this moment and will “never forget” my traitorous attitude.

I expect nothing less.

Posterity will rightfully judge us all for how we respond to these wanton
acts, the consequences of which will most likely have a ripple effect upon
them years from now. The U.S. and Israeli attack on Iran threatens the very
foundation of collective ethics and international law. The disgraceful
flaunting of the rule of law sets a calamitous precedent moving forward. It
opens a Pandora’s Box of potential lawlessness on a global scale, one in which
“might makes right.” It may very well take years for civilization to claw its
way back to the ethical baseline that tenuously existed before February 28.
Our children absolutely should hold us accountable for our stance and public
response today.

We, in turn, should demand the same from our leaders, including the shameful
initial endorsements of this illegality from middle powers such as the
[E3](https://www.gov.uk/government/news/joint-e3-leaders-statement-on-
iran-28-february-2026) and [Australia](https://www.pm.gov.au/media/statement-
iran). Here in[ Canada](https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/iran-united-states-
canada-carney-9.7111856), the best that my own Prime Minister, Mark Carney,
could muster in walking back his tacit support for the February 28 attacks was
to add that he did so “with some regret” over its apparent violation of
international order. He then subsequently
[indicated](https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/livestory/conflict-with-
iran-9.7109761) that he would not rule out Canada’s participation in this
criminal endeavor.

When I publicly opposed the Gaza genocide last year, many others treated me as
if I wore a veritable “[Mark of
Cain](https://www.jurist.org/commentary/2025/08/bearing-the-mark-of-cain-for-
naming-the-gaza-genocide/).” A similar pattern is likely to emerge now, once
many colleagues in the circles I frequent read this commentary. Already, I
have lost count of how many times my coreligionists have labelled me a
“[kapo](https://encyclopedia.ushmm.org/content/en/article/kapos-and-other-
prisoner-functionaries-in-nazi-concentration-camps)” for my views, comparing
me to Jewish concentration camp inmates who served the SS guards and betrayed
their fellow Jews. If I end up reprising a villainous role in the minds of
such critics, so be it. There is far too much at stake for humanity’s welfare
to remain silent and risk normalizing such egregious, opportunistic displays
of power.

If we cannot unravel this tightening Gordian knot of tyranny in our lifetimes,
the very least we can do is proclaim our response in the public record as
fervently as possible. The hope is that our pleas might inspire our progeny to
find a way to mend the broken world we will have left them. This testament is
my best attempt at that implicit charge to posterity.

There is a well-known aphorism from an ancient Jewish text entitled Pirkei
Avot (Ethics of the Fathers). Rabbi Tarfon asserts: “It is not your duty to
finish the work, but neither are you at liberty to neglect it.”
[(2:16)](https://www.sefaria.org/Pirkei_Avot.2.16) May we each do our part in
sounding the alarm loudly enough to motivate our descendants to help reckon
with the disastrous fallout of this latest chapter in humanity’s ruinous march
of folly, once and for all.

And may our offspring heed this call.
